title: Shared VPC Egress & IP Management for GPU Workloads
author: Sofia Patel
content:
Summary:
This page documents the shared VPC topology, egress control, and IP address management patterns for GPU-backed inference and training workloads. It codifies Terraform module usage, CI/CD safety gates, and an operational runbook for network egress or NAT gateway incidents. The goal is to provide reproducible, auditable network constructs that minimize blast radius and simplify IP/cost allocation for multi-tenant GPU clusters.

Scope:
- Applies to all GPU clusters (hosted and dedicated) that attach to our shared VPCs (prod-shared-vpc, staging-shared-vpc).
- Covers egress (NAT / egress proxies), static IP allocation for model-serving endpoints, and Terraform patterns for cross-project attachments.
- Does NOT cover per-customer private-only on-prem stacks (see eng-private-deployments/reference-architectures).

Goals and non‑goals:
- Goals:
  - Ensure deterministic, billable egress paths for GPU workloads with minimal changes to existing GKE/AKS/EKS node pools.
  - Provide reusable Terraform modules for attaching GPU subnets to shared VPCs and reserving static egress IPs.
  - Enable rapid rollback and isolation during network incidents.
- Non‑goals:
  - Replace per-customer VPN connectivity designs.

Owners and stakeholders:
- Primary owner: infra-networking (team lead: Evan Morales)
- Secondary stakeholders: eng-serving-runtime (oncall), eng-infra-sre, security-compliance
- Approvers for changes: infra-networking, eng-sre, security for restricted changes

Design overview:
We use a shared VPC model. GPU clusters live in project-scoped clusters that attach their node subnets to the shared VPC via VPC peering / Shared VPC attachment (cloud provider specific). Egress is funneled through a controlled set of NAT gateways or centralized egress appliances (egress-proxy pods / proxy instances) that present static public IPs.

High-level ASCII topology:

  Internet
     |
  [Global LB / CDN]
     |
  [Egress NAT pool / EgressProxy]
     |
  Shared VPC (prod-shared-vpc)
     |-- subnet-gpu-1 (10.40.16.0/20)  <-- GPU node pools (project: gpu-prod-01)
     |-- subnet-gpu-2 (10.40.32.0/20)  <-- GPU node pools (project: gpu-prod-02)
     |-- subnet-services (10.40.0.0/22) <-- control plane, logging
IP allocation table (example):
| Logical name          | CIDR              | Purpose                          | Owner project            | Notes |
|-----------------------|-------------------|----------------------------------|--------------------------|-------|
| subnet-gpu-1          | 10.40.16.0/20     | GPU nodes (infer/serving)        | gpu-prod-01              | reserved for GPU autoscale groups |
| subnet-gpu-2          | 10.40.32.0/20     | GPU nodes (training/batch)       | gpu-prod-02              | pre-alloc to reduce fragmentation |
| subnet-services       | 10.40.0.0/22      | Logging, metrics, proxies        | infra-services           | hosts egress proxies, logging forwarders |
| nat-pool-prod         | N/A (public IPs)  | Static egress IPs (5x)           | infra-networking         | allocated in cloud provider, tagged cost-center=infra |

Firewall / egress policy matrix (summary):
| From                 | To                   | Ports/protocols           | Rationale / rule id |
|----------------------|----------------------|---------------------------|--------------------|
| subnet-gpu-*         | Internet (via NAT)   | 443,80                    | Allow outbound to pull images / external APIs (RULE-EG-01) |
| subnet-gpu-*         | 10.40.0.0/22         | 10250 (kubelet), 22       | Cluster control plane and bastion (RULE-INTRA-02) |
| subnet-services      | External telemetry   | 443                       | Metrics export to external SaaS (RULE-EG-03) |
| 0.0.0.0/0            | nat-pool-prod        | Managed                    | Only NAT-managed egress allowed (RULE-EG-00) |

Terraform & IaC patterns:
- Use centralized terraform modules in //terraform/modules/shared-vpc (registry: internal-terraform) to manage anchors: subnets, route tables, firewall rules, static IPs.
- Per-cluster terraform lives in project-level repos and should reference the module via versioned module source. Avoid inlining shared VPC resources in per-project stacks.
- Naming conventions: module outputs must provide: shared_vpc_id, subnet_ids, nat_static_ips[]. Tags: { "team": "infra-networking", "env": "prod", "cost_center": "gpu" }

Example module usage (pseudo-Terraform):
```
module "gpu_shared_vpc_attachment" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@internal/terraform/modules/shared-vpc.git//attachments"
  version = "v1.4.2"

  project_id = var.project_id
  cluster_subnet_cidrs = ["10.40.16.0/20"]
  requested_static_ips = 2
  labels = {
    team = "infra-networking"
    env = var.env
  }
}
```

CI/CD: safe apply patterns for network changes:
1) All terraform changes to shared-vpc modules require an RFC PR with: plan output, impact statement (which IP blocks changed), tag of approvers.
2) Merge triggers a pipeline: terraform plan -> security scan (check for opening 0.0.0.0/0 rules) -> plan approval (manual) -> apply in a single control-plane account.
3) Applies to nat-pool changes require break-glass key rotation steps documented and explicit approve from infra-networking + security.

Example pipeline guardrails (GitHub Actions / GitLab CI):
- Stage: format & lint
- Stage: terraform plan (outputs saved artifact)
- Stage: iam / policy scan (opa/terrascan)
- Approval: manual with at least two approvers (infra-networking + eng-sre)
- Stage: apply (runs from bastion CI runner with limited key and remote-state locking)

Operational runbook: egress degraded / NAT pool exhausted
1) Symptoms: external calls from gpu nodes fail with 403/timeout or new connections queue behind SNAT shortage. Alerts: SNAT exhaustion alert (see Monitoring).
2) Immediate mitigation (15 min):
   a) Confirm alert via logs: grep for SNAT failures in logging-forwarder or cloud NAT metrics.
   b) If NAT pool exhausted: temporarily attach additional static IPs from nat-pool reserve using IaC module (run terraform apply with requested_static_ips +1).
   c) If attaching IPs not possible (quota): route outbound from critical clusters to egress-proxy nodes in subnet-services (manual route change):
      - Update route table to send traffic for 0.0.0.0/0 from affected subnet to egress-proxy instance group (put into maintenance mode first).
   d) If traffic needs to be blocked, implement emergency deny rules at firewall (RULE-EG-EMERG) to isolate affected projects.
3) Post-incident: run IP allocation tidy-up, increase NAT quotas, and open RFC to expand nat-pool.

Testing and validation checklist (pre-merge):
- terraform plan shows only expected resources changed
- integration test: deploy small GKE nodepool into a test shared-vpc attachment and run `curl https://ifconfig.co` from a GPU pod to verify static IP presented matches nat-pool mapping
- iptables/snat sanity: run `kubectl exec` to check conntrack stats and ephemeral port usage on a sample pod

Monitoring and alerts (owners):
- Metric: nat.active_port_count / nat.free_ports (infra-networking)
  - Alert: nat.free_ports < 100 => P2 (notify infra-networking Slack #infra-alerts)
  - Alert: nat.free_ports == 0 => P1 (phone escalation to oncall)
- Metric: egress-proxy 5xx rate > 1% over 5m => P2 (eng-serving-runtime)
- Dashboards: shared-vpc / nat / egress-proxy error budget, utilization graphs (Grafana linked to Prometheus / Cloud Monitoring)

Tagging & billing: conventions for GPU projects
- Required tags on all static IP resources: [team, env, cost_center, business_unit]
- GPU clusters should include cost tags: {"accelerator": "A100", "workload": "inference"}
- Billing owner must be set in terraform var owner_email for every project-level stack to allow automated chargeback in FinOps reports.

Gradual rollout checklist for changing egress path:
1) Create change RFC and include smoke-test plan and roll-forward/rollback steps.
2) Deploy change to staging-shared-vpc and run 48h soak with synthetic traffic (image pulls, embeddings API calls).
3) Apply to one non-critical GPU project (gpu-canary) and verify metrics for 6h.
4) Schedule migration window for remaining projects; communicate to stakeholders 48h prior.

Security considerations:
- All NAT static IPs must be rotatable; document rotation process and automate TTL-based replacement every 180 days where applicable.
- Egress proxies should enforce outbound allow-listing by service-account and purpose; secrets for proxies stored in KMS and vaulted by SecretsManager.
- Any rule opening inbound access to GPU subnets must be elevated to restricted confidentiality and approved by Security.

Appendix: useful commands
- Verify current static IPs (GCP example):
  gcloud compute addresses list --filter="labels.cost_center:gpu" --project=infra-networking
- Check NAT metrics (Cloud Monitoring):
  gcloud monitoring time-series list --project=infra-monitoring --filter='metric.type="compute.googleapis.com/instance/network/egress_bytes_count"' --limit=10
- From a pod, check external IP seen:
  kubectl run --rm -it --image=alpine:3.17 snat-test -- sh -c "apk add --no-cache curl; curl -s https://ifconfig.co"
